framework.name: NIST SP 800-207 Zero Trust
framework.description: NIST SP 800-207 defines the Zero Trust Architecture (ZTA) model, providing a set of tenets that serve as the foundation for designing and deploying zero trust enterprise networks. It shifts security focus from network perimeter defense to resource-level protection.

controls.title: All Data Sources and Computing Services Are Considered Resources
controls.description: All data sources and computing services are considered resources.

questions: How does your architecture inventory every data source and computing service so that each one is treated as a protected resource?
What mechanism ensures that newly deployed services, databases, and SaaS applications are automatically registered as resources subject to zero trust policy?
Where does your policy engine obtain its authoritative list of resources when it evaluates an access request?
How do policy enforcement points mediate access to non-traditional resources such as APIs and serverless functions, not just servers and applications?
Who owns the process for classifying data sources and computing services as enterprise resources, and how often is that classification reviewed?
What criteria determine whether an asset falls within the scope of your zero trust resource definition?
How does your decommissioning process ensure retired services are removed from the resource inventory and their access policies revoked?

controls.title: All Communication Is Secured Regardless of Network Location
controls.description: All communication is secured regardless of network location.

questions: What encryption and authentication controls protect traffic between internal services, and how do they compare with the protections applied to external connections?
How does your architecture prevent implicit trust for requests that originate on enterprise-owned network infrastructure?
Which technologies, such as mutual TLS or encrypted overlays, secure communication in transit across every network segment?
How are legacy systems that cannot support encrypted transport identified, and what compensating controls protect their traffic?
How do you detect unencrypted or improperly authenticated traffic within your environment?
What monitoring confirms that confidentiality and integrity protections stay in place as workloads move between on-premises and cloud locations?
How are exceptions to the secure communication requirement recorded, risk-assessed, and tracked to closure?

controls.title: Per-Session Access to Individual Enterprise Resources
controls.description: Access to individual enterprise resources is granted on a per-session basis.

questions: How does your policy enforcement point grant access to a single resource for a single session rather than issuing broad, long-lived network access?
What limits session lifetime, and what triggers a fresh trust evaluation before a new session to the same resource is established?
How do you ensure that access granted to one enterprise resource does not automatically extend to other resources?
How is least privilege applied when scoping the permissions granted within an individual session?
What policy defines acceptable session durations and re-authentication thresholds for resources of different sensitivity levels?
How do you confirm that the entitlements evaluated at session establishment reflect a user's current role and need?
Who approves any deviation that permits persistent or multi-resource sessions, and how are those decisions revisited?

controls.title: Dynamic Policy-Based Resource Access
controls.description: Access to resources is determined by dynamic policy -- including the observable state of client identity, application/service, and the requesting asset -- and may include other behavioral and environmental attributes.

questions: Which attributes of client identity, the application or service, and the requesting asset does your policy engine evaluate when deciding an access request?
How are behavioral and environmental attributes, such as location or usage patterns, incorporated into dynamic access decisions?
How does the policy engine obtain the observable state of the requesting asset, such as software version or patch level, at decision time?
How quickly do changes in identity or device state propagate into the policies applied to subsequent access requests?
Where are your dynamic access policies documented, and how do they show the attributes and rules the policy engine applies?
What records demonstrate that a specific access decision was based on the client, application, and asset state observed at the time of the request?
How do you document changes to policy rules, and what evidence shows they were tested before enforcement?

controls.title: Integrity and Security Posture Monitoring of All Assets
controls.description: The enterprise monitors and measures the integrity and security posture of all owned and associated assets.

questions: What tooling continuously measures the integrity and security posture of enterprise-owned and associated assets?
How is posture data, such as patch level and configuration state, fed into the policy engine that decides resource access?
How does your access control plane treat assets whose measured posture has degraded or that carry known vulnerabilities?
How do you monitor devices your enterprise does not own but that are associated with access to enterprise resources?
How do you identify assets that appear subverted, lack expected patches, or fall outside your monitoring coverage?
What thresholds trigger denial or restriction of access based on an asset's measured security posture?
How is monitoring coverage itself measured so that gaps in asset visibility are surfaced and remediated?

controls.title: Dynamic Authentication and Authorization Enforcement
controls.description: All resource authentication and authorization are dynamic and strictly enforced before access is allowed.

questions: How are authentication and authorization enforced before every resource access rather than only at initial network entry?
What mechanisms support re-evaluating trust during an ongoing session, such as reauthentication triggers or continuous risk scoring?
How does your identity, credential, and access management stack integrate with policy enforcement points so decisions are applied in real time?
How is multifactor authentication applied dynamically based on the sensitivity of the requested resource?
What policy governs the ongoing cycle of granting access, assessing threats, and re-evaluating trust for active sessions?
How are the criteria for stepping up authentication or revoking access decided, and who approves them?
How do you verify that enforcement is strict, meaning no access paths exist that bypass authentication and authorization checks?

controls.title: Comprehensive Data Collection for Security Posture Improvement
controls.description: The enterprise collects as much information as possible about the current state of assets, network infrastructure and communications and uses it to improve its security posture.

questions: What information do you collect about the current state of assets, network infrastructure, and communications across the enterprise?
How is the collected data analyzed to produce insight that improves policy creation and enforcement?
How does this telemetry refine the policy engine's access decisions over time?
What gaps exist in your current collection coverage, and how are they being addressed?
What records show that insight from collected data has led to concrete improvements in your security posture or access policies?
How is the data collection scope documented, including the systems in scope and retention periods for the telemetry?
What evidence demonstrates a working feedback loop between operational telemetry and policy updates?
